column3: You asked for the truth. So this time, you tell it.
I met him on a train, ten minutes ago.
Then you go in. He stays out.
Eli doesn't argue. He almost looks relieved.
That's exactly what I wanted. Now take this case to the kids.
He shoves you through the gap. The last thing you see is him, sitting down against the door.
Then the flash. Even through all that steel, the whole shelter shakes.
You hand out his pills. Forty packets. Forty kids.
That's my husband's case. Where did you get it?
So you tell her the truth. Again.
My husband called me an hour ago. A stranger pulled him from a burning car.
He gave that man his card. He said he'd save more people than he ever could.
On the door camera, Eli gets up, walks to the old wall phone, and makes one more call.
Twenty-four hours later, the door opens. The corridor is empty.
Just his hoodie, folded on the floor. And a note.
Your sister's safe. Go find her.
The truth cost him the door. But Eli was never trying to get in.
So where did he go? Follow for season two.
